title: Geopolitics and foreign holdings of euro area government debt
summary: ECB staff research using granular Securities Holdings Statistics (SHS) data examines how foreign holdings of euro area government debt react to geopolitical factors since Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Foreign investors hold approximately 24% of euro area government debt, with foreign official sector holdings concentrated in geopolitically non-aligned countries. While official foreign holdings have remained generally resilient post-invasion, econometric estimates suggest geopolitical non-alignment explains at least part of the 5% decline in holdings from non-aligned countries relative to pre-invasion levels.
key_points: Foreign investors hold nearly 24% of both euro area and US government debt (euro area total: €11,186.3bn in government debt securities; non-resident holdings: €2,591.5bn per IIP, €2,674.2bn per SHS)
Foreign official sector holdings of euro area government debt are mainly held by countries geopolitically non-aligned with the West
Official foreign holdings of euro area debt have remained generally resilient since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine
Holdings by non-aligned countries (excluding Russia) have declined by 5% relative to pre-invasion levels, a decline partially explained by geopolitical non-alignment in econometric estimates
Foreign official sector holdings: €952.4bn (per ECB SHS), representing a subset of total foreign holdings of €2,674.2bn
The impact on euro area bond yields has been very limited thus far due to the small magnitude of the decline
why_it_matters: Foreign holdings of sovereign debt affect borrowing costs and monetary policy transmission. Sudden reversals in foreign holdings could destabilize sovereign bond markets, as seen during the euro area sovereign debt crisis. Understanding how geopolitics influences official sector holdings is critical for assessing euro area bond market resilience and the international role of the euro. The resilience of official foreign holdings since 2022 is a positive signal for euro area sovereign debt market stability.
market_structure_context: The paper provides granular data on the composition of euro area sovereign debt holders by geography and sector (official vs. private). It highlights the role of foreign official investors (central banks, sovereign wealth funds, international organizations) in euro area bond markets. The analysis corrects for geographic biases in international financial statistics. The SHS data only covers holdings with euro area custodians, potentially undercounting holdings via non-euro area custodians. The paper notes a custodial bias in US TICS data that does not look through holdings in European financial centers.
important_numbers: 24% foreign ownership of euro area government debt
€11,186.3bn total euro area government debt securities (Q4 2024)
5% decline in holdings by non-aligned countries (excluding Russia) relative to pre-invasion levels
notes: Historical record (published June 2025, approximately 10 months before TODAY). Source is high-quality ECB staff research using granular custodial data (SHS). Truncated during extraction; some data tables and additional analysis may not be captured. Key finding: geopolitical non-alignment is an explanatory factor for declines in official foreign holdings but impact on yields has been limited. This is a research paper from the 'International role of the euro' series, authored by Beck, Burian, Georgiadis, and McQuade. Author names confirmed in source body.
